label: China announces Project 985 to build world-class universities
detail: Announced May 1998; nine universities at first, 39 in all.

label: Shanghai ranking (ARWU) first published
detail: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, June 2003. Its initial purpose: to find the global standing of top Chinese universities.

label: Elsevier launches Scopus
detail: Launched 3 November 2004 in London.

label: First THE–QS world ranking
detail: November 2004, Times Higher Education Supplement with QS, 200 universities.

label: THE–QS ranking uses Scopus data for the first time
detail: Published 9 November 2007.

label: SCImago Journal & Country Rank launched
detail: Announced 24 November 2007; built on Scopus data. Source of the Q1–Q4 quartiles.

label: THE chooses Elsevier (Scopus) as its data supplier
detail: November 2014, replacing Thomson Reuters.

label: China plans world-class universities by 2020
detail: Announced November 2015.

lane: Indonesia: scoring of people, journals and universities
label: SINTA launched
detail: Version 1.0 launched 30 January 2017 at UGM; version 2.0 on 4 August 2017.

label: Lecturer allowances tied to publishing (Permenristekdikti 20/2017)
detail: Permenristekdikti 20/2017: tunjangan profesi and tunjangan kehormatan (2x base salary) tied to 3-year publication duty; LK: 3 accredited national or 1 international. Rewards: Publication count and venue tier over 3 years

label: Professors told to publish internationally to keep their allowance
detail: Professors told to meet reputable-international duty by Nov 2019 to keep the honorarium allowance. Rewards: Reputable international journal article

label: Promotion points: 40 for a Scopus/WoS article, 25 for a top national one
detail: PO PAK 2019 credit points per article: 40 Scopus/WoS reputable; 30 international; 25 SINTA 1-2; 20 SINTA 3-4; 15 SINTA 5-6/DOAJ; 10 other. Rewards: Indexing tier of the journal

lane: Indonesia: money for articles and journals
label: Ministry incentive for Scopus/WoS articles (up to Rp35m)
detail: Insentif Artikel guide, Kemenristekdikti (max Rp35m; non-lecturer researchers). Rewards: Scopus/WoS article; scored on impact factor/h-index of journal and citation count of article

label: Professor rank needs a reputable international article; SJR above 0.1
detail: PO PAK 2019 special requirement (SE 638/E.E4/KP/2020): professor needs first-author reputable international article; leaps need 2 (to LK) or 4 (to GB), half above field-average SJR (arts/humanities 0.25; social 0.40). Rewards: Scopus SJR > 0.1 or WoS JIF >= 0.05; field-average SJR for fast-track

lane: Indonesia: scoring of people, journals and universities
label: University clustering counts indexed articles and citations per lecturer
detail: Klasterisasi Perguruan Tinggi (5 clusters, 2,136 institutions). Rewards: Output: indexed articles per lecturer; outcome: citations per lecturer

lane: Indonesia: scoring of people, journals and universities
label: Doctoral programme accreditation rewards reputable international articles
detail: BAN-PT IAPS 4.0 doctoral instrument (PerBAN-PT 2/2020): full score if >= 3% of student outputs in reputable international journals; professor share. Rewards: Student publication ratios; professors among staff

lane: Indonesia: scoring of people, journals and universities
label: Journal accreditation scores citations and international indexing
detail: Journal accreditation (Kepdirjen 134/E/KPT/2021): 'dampak ilmiah' element. Rewards: Citations from other journals over 3 years, impact factor and/or h-index; points for international indexing

lane: Indonesia: scoring of people, journals and universities
label: Journal accreditation prescribes the abstract and article formula
detail: Same guideline (Kepdirjen 134/E/KPT/2021, Lampiran p. 15), 'Gaya Penulisan': the abstract must at least contain 'tujuan kajian, metode singkat, hasil temuan singkat, dan simpulan singkat' (aim, brief method, brief findings, brief conclusion); article structure 'terdiri atas pendahuluan, metode, hasil dan pembahasan, dan simpulan' (introduction, method, results and discussion, conclusion), with an exception only for 'bidang ilmu tertentu' and review articles. Both are scored in the accreditation instrument (Tabel 7).

label: Award for the Islamic university with the most Scopus journals
detail: Anugerah Diktis (ADIKTIS): 'PTKI with most Scopus-indexed journals' and 'most reputable journals'. Rewards: Count of Scopus journals owned

lane: Indonesia: money for articles and journals
label: Grants to help journals move toward international indexing
detail: Bantuan Pengelolaan Jurnal Ilmiah (DRTPM): accredited track up to Rp50m; 'towards reputable international index' track up to Rp62.5m. Rewards: SINTA rank; international editors/reviewers; readiness for Scopus

label: Publication assistance, including for reputable international journals
detail: Diktis publication assistance, nine clusters incl. awards for reputable international journals (1,496 proposals). Rewards: Reputable international journal status

label: Credit points reset to institution-assessed performance (Permenpan RB 1/2023)
detail: Permenpan RB 1/2023: lecturer credit points reset to institution-assessed performance; pre-2023 credits converted. Rewards: Performance assessed by institution using SINTA, BIMA, SISTER data

label: Award up to Rp40m per Scopus/WoS article
detail: Litapdimas: Penghargaan Penulis Artikel di Jurnal Internasional Bereputasi, up to Rp40m. Rewards: Scopus/WoS article within 3 years

label: Professor publication defined as Scopus SJR 0.15 or more
detail: Kepmendikbudristek 500/M/2024: professor publication = Scopus SJR >= 0.15 or WoS JIF >= 0.05, editors from >= 4 countries, authors from >= 2 countries per issue. Rewards: SJR threshold; internationality of journal

lane: Indonesia: scoring of people, journals and universities
label: SINTA score: Scopus Q1 article 24 points, each Scopus citation 1 point
detail: SINTA score (lecturer, department, institution; 3-year and overall). Rewards: Scopus Q1 first author 24 pts ... Q4 18; SINTA-1/2 article 15; Scopus citations 1 pt each; Scopus cited documents 5 pts each

label: Target to lift Islamic state universities into QS top 300–400
detail: Kemenag target to lift PTKIN in QS WUR to ~300-400; eight UIN pilots; lecturer certification quota 2,000 -> 5,000. Rewards: QS rank

label: New lecturer career regulation (Permendiktisaintek 52/2025)
detail: Permendiktisaintek 52/2025: LK needs >= 1 scientific publication (40% research credits); professor >= 2 (45%); rank-skipping allowed again. Rewards: Publication count; indexing criteria delegated (not verified)

lane: Indonesia: money for articles and journals
label: National article incentive: Q1 and Q2 only
detail: Insentif Artikel Berkualitas pada Jurnal Internasional Bereputasi (letter 1640/C3/DT.05.00/2025). Rewards: Article in Scopus/WoS Q1 or Q2 journal; amount not stated in letter

lane: Indonesia: money for articles and journals
label: Incentive for journals whose quartile or SJR rises
detail: Insentif Peningkatan Kualitas / Pengelolaan Jurnal Elektronik (letter 1641/C3/DT.05.00/2025). Rewards: Year-on-year rise in Scopus/WoS quartile, SJR or JIF, or SINTA rank; size scales with latest quartile

lane: Indonesia: money for articles and journals
label: Top-10% Scopus journals: up to Rp30m per article (EQUITY)
detail: EQUITY-WCU (LPDP endowment) 'Top Tier' publication incentive, up to Rp30m per article (UI implementation). Rewards: Article in a journal in the top 10% of its Scopus sub-subject

lane: Indonesia: scoring of people, journals and universities
label: World Class University programme celebrates a 46% rise in QS positions
detail: World Class University programme; ministry celebrates 46% rise in QS positions. Rewards: QS World University Rankings position

label: Promotion guidelines define a reputable journal by Scopus: Q4, Q3, Q2 by rank
detail: Kepmendiktisaintek 39/M/KEP/2026 (26 Jan 2026): reputable international journal = indexed in Scopus with SJR above 0.1, or WoS IF above 0.05. Lektor Q4+, Lektor Kepala Q3+, Profesor Q2+ plus Q3+; national accredited journals allowed as an alternative.

lane: Indonesia: money for articles and journals
label: RINJANI: 144 Indonesian Scopus journals pushed toward Q1
detail: Program RINJANI: acceleration of 144 Scopus-indexed Indonesian journals toward Q1. Rewards: Quartile upgrade; performance contracts; planned rewards for top authors
